originalTitle: Hundreds of far-right protesters descend on Portsmouth after small boat arrival
summary: Influencer livestreams event calling for men to travel to port to block coaches carrying asylum seekers from leaving
content: Hundreds of far-right activists have descended on Portsmouth, where a small boat with 140 asylum seekers on board was intercepted heading towards the Portsmouth coast. The vessel’s arrival sparked a major response with a helicopter, an aeroplane and lifeboats sent to the scene. It is thought to be the first time such a large boat containing asylum seekers has been brought to Portsmouth and the first time a large group of anti-migrant protesters have tried to block newly arrived asylum seekers from being processed. The protesters blocked roads for hours and vowed to stay all night to prevent the new arrivals from being taken to a processing centre. It is the second major anti-migrant protest of the weekend. Many of those at Portsmouth were dressed in all black and wore face masks, similar to those who attended a rally that blocked roads in Dover on Saturday. One witness who was not involved in the protest said on Sunday night: “The atmosphere here is still very tense. The coaches carrying asylum seekers have still not left. About 25-30% of the far-right protesters are wearing balaclavas and many are wearing black. Two police cars had their windscreens smashed by protesters. At one point they broke through the police cordon.” The boat’s occupants were brought to shore in the maritime city and the Home Office’s plan was to take them to Manston, outside Ramsgate in Kent, where small boat arrivals are processed. However, videos circulating on social media showed large groups of protesters close to the coaches that were to be used, with some blocking vehicles carrying asylum seekers from leaving. Hampshire police urged people to avoid the area, and said a dispersal order was in place. The government has condemned what it described as the “thuggish behaviour” of the protesters. “We condemn the intimidating and thuggish behaviour we are seeing tonight,” a government spokesperson said. “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but it must never cross a line into disorder.” In a livestream from the scene, Daniel Thomas, also known as Danny Tommo – a former bodyguard of the far-right activist Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon – encouraged viewers to travel to Portsmouth to join the protest. Thomas has recently established Patriot Platform which blocked part of port of Dover on Saturday. He previously launched Operation Overlord which planned to send far-right activists to France to “stop the boats”. He and his supporters filmed themselves slashing abandoned dinghies on a French beach. The french authorities subsequently banned him from France. Small boat crossings so far this year have reduced by more than 40% compared with the same period last year. While the Home Office has disrupted the smugglers’ business model, their methods appear to have evolved by launching boats such as the one that arrived on Sunday evening from different parts of the coast, much further from the UK, making the crossings more dangerous. Most small boat arrivals are rescued by Border Force and RNLI boats on the English side of the Channel and brought ashore in Dover. A Maritime and Coastguard Agency spokesperson said: “In response to a report on 6 September of a small boat heading towards the Hampshire coast, HM Coastguard sent lifeboats, an HM Coastguard helicopter, an HM Coastguard aeroplane and HM Coastguard Rescue Teams. “Border Force, Border Security Command, Hampshire police and south central ambulance service were also sent.” Stand Up To Racism posted on X: “another attempt by fascist Danny Tommo to whip up pogroms against refugees.” A Home Office spokesperson said: “This government is bearing down on dangerous small boat crossings and restoring control at our border. Joint efforts have seen over 48,000 crossing attempts prevented and 1,100 boats and engines seized since the election. “We are making progress, with the number of small boat crossings down this year and the lowest number recorded for the month of July since 2020. “But we must go further, which is why we have signed a payment-by-results deal with the French to put 40% more boots on the ground on French beaches.”
chineseTitle: 小船抵达后，数百名极右翼抗议者涌向朴茨茅斯
chineseSummary: 有影响力的直播活动呼吁男性前往港口阻止载有寻求庇护者的教练离开
chineseContent: 数百名极右翼活动人士涌入朴茨茅斯，一艘载有 140 名寻求庇护者的小船在驶向朴茨茅斯海岸时被拦截。该船的到来引起了强烈反响，一架直升机、一架飞机和救生艇被派往现场。据信，这是第一次载有如此大的寻求庇护者的船只被带到朴茨茅斯，也是第一次有一大群反移民抗议者试图阻止新抵达的寻求庇护者接受处理。抗议者封锁道路数小时，并发誓要留守过夜，以防止新来者被带到处理中心。这是周末第二次重大反移民抗议活动。朴茨茅斯的许多人都穿着全黑衣服，戴着口罩，类似于周六参加多佛封锁道路集会的人。一名未参与抗议活动的目击者周日晚上表示：“这里的气氛仍然非常紧张。载着寻求庇护者的大巴还没有离开。大约25-30%的极右抗议者戴着巴拉克拉法帽，其中许多人穿着黑色衣服。两辆警车的挡风玻璃被抗议者砸碎。他们一度冲破了警方的警戒线。”船上的乘客被带到这座海上城市的岸边，内政部的计划是将他们带到肯特郡拉姆斯盖特郊外的曼斯顿，在那里处理小船的抵达。然而，社交媒体上流传的视频显示，大批抗议者靠近要使用的巴士，其中一些人阻止载有寻求庇护者的车辆离开。汉普郡警方敦促人们避开该地区，并表示已经发布了驱散令。政府谴责抗议者的“暴行行为”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
